summary: Eleven connected diplomatic-dispatch and memorial source-context repairs: retain existing AD346 one-sided bounds and make their narrative basis explicit. Partial uninstalled proposal; no date approval.

sourceDate.text: 訪以詔書付賈陵

before.event: Geng Fang handed the edict to Jia Ling of Longxi, who was to pose as a merchant.
before.unresolvedReason: The handing of the edict follows the seven-year stay and precedes 以咸和八年始達涼州.

sourceDate.text: 訪以詔書付賈陵，托為賈客 (s0465), preceding 以咸和八年始達涼州 (s0466, conventional AD333); handover year unstated

after.event: Geng Fang handed the edict to Jia Ling of Longxi, who was to pose as a merchant.

changes.reason: s0465 explicitly names Jia Ling as the recipient of the edict Geng Fang hands over, with instructions to pose as a merchant. s0466 continues his journey through Chang’an to the eventual Liangzhou arrival explicitly dated 咸和八年. Thus the handover must be onOrBefore the existing conventional AD333 arrival-year ceiling. s0464’s seven-year stay is retained as context, but its endpoints and counting convention are not inferred. This dates Jia Ling’s own receipt of the edict conservatively; it is not an exact handover year, whole activity interval, or a conversion of 至是.

This is Qu Hu’s own mission in the narrative after conventional Xianhe9/AD334, supporting the existing lower bound. 後 does not identify Xiankang1 or any exact mission year, and annual missions do not supply its duration or a latest endpoint.

after.event: Qu Hu’s memorial says that after Shi Le and Li Xiong died, Li Qi and Shi Hu usurped the line and glared like owls for years.

changes.reason: s0470 introduces the current memorial carried by Qu Hu after the 九年 heading of s0468. s0477 contrasts Shi Le and Li Xiong already dead with Jilong and Li Qi having succeeded violently and remained threatening for years; s0478 and the requested current campaign in s0484 continue that present danger. The event remains a contemporary memorial’s attestation of Li Qi’s ongoing rule, not a claim assigning his entire reign to the speech year. The existing onOrAfter AD334 floor dates that attestation; 有年 is an unnumbered duration and provides neither an exact usurpation year nor a reign endpoint.

The sentence then names Yu Liang as the grand general who memorializes for the envoys’ appointment, so this is his own current advocacy rather than a date inferred from his tenure. The underlying 九年 heading at s0468 follows 咸和八年 in s0466, supporting the retained onOrAfter conventional AD334 floor. Keep the next named 永和元年 heading as context, without replacing 後 by a precise year or importing Yu Liang’s whole office span.

The existing onOrAfter AD334 lower bound is supported for Chen Yu’s own mission and appointment. No Xiankang4 or exact calendar year is stated; the next named 永和元年 heading remains visible without becoming an invented event year.
